cues: Steel is iron with its carbon cut to between a quarter and one and a half percent, and the silicon, manganese, phosphorus and sulphur removed.
Most of the world's steel is made by the basic oxygen process.
Molten pig iron, scrap and quicklime go into a pear shaped converter with a basic lining of dolomite.
A water cooled lance blows pure oxygen onto the melt.
text: Steel is iron with its carbon cut to between a quarter and one and a half percent, and the silicon, manganese, phosphorus and sulphur removed.
